claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or children aged 16-19 who are still in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 19 and he's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know that Alex is 19 and still in college doing A-levels, which counts as approved education.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to understand your living situation:

**Do you live with Alex, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you. Since Alex lives with you, that's an important factor for eligibility.

Now I need to ask about your immigration or residency status, as this can affect Child Benefit eligibility:

**What is your current residency status in the UK? For example, are you a UK citizen, do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or something else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a UK citizen, yes. I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. As a UK citizen living in the UK, that satisfies the residency requirement.

Now I have one more important question to complete the assessment:

**Is there anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else agreed to claim Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me - I'm his only parent claiming anything for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me:
- You're a UK citizen living in Manchester
- You live with Alex
- Alex is 19 and currently in approved education (A-levels at college)
- You're his only parent claiming for him
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for Alex. The key requirements are satisfied:
1. You're responsible for him (you live with him)
2. You live in the UK
3. He's under 20 and in approved education or training
4. Only you are claiming for him

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex!**

You meet all the necessary requirements to claim Child Benefit. If you haven't already done so, you can make a claim through the usual channels. Remember that Child Benefit will normally continue while Alex remains in approved education or training and is under 20 years old.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your eligibility?
